title: Pradeep Singh v. IndiGo Airlines
text: The complainant, Pradeep Singh, missed his connecting international flight due to a delay caused by the opposite party airline. The airline failed to provide timely alternate arrangements, leaving the complainant stranded at the transit airport for 36 hours. The complainant incurred additional hotel and travel expenses of Rs 1,50,000. A consumer complaint was filed before NCDRC alleging deficiency in service. The opposite party attributed the delay to bad weather, which is a force majeure event. The NCDRC examined the DGCA circulars and found that even during weather delays, the airline has obligations to provide accommodation and meals to stranded passengers. Failure to do so constitutes deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act. The complainant is awarded Rs 1,50,000 as reimbursement and Rs 1,00,000 as compensation for inconvenience and mental agony.
